due_when.clears_when: Either (a) the backlog guards detect a whole-file re-serialization and say so explicitly — e.g. when the added-line count exceeds some large fraction of the file, report 'this looks like a reformat, not N new rows' and grade against the PARSED rows rather than the diff lines, so the message names the real cause; or (b) a guard fails a PR that re-serializes a backlog with different json.dumps options, pointing at scripts/ops/backlog_append.py, which already carries a style-detection candidate list for exactly this and is the tool a session should be reaching for. (a) is the more useful of the two because it fixes the misleading MESSAGE, which is the costly part. Verified by a test that reformats a fixture backlog and asserts the guard's output names the reformat rather than listing rows.
